title: Thrissur Pooram
description: Kerala's best-known temple festival, with caparisoned elephants, percussion ensembles and fireworks.
date_note: Held on the Pooram day of the Malayalam month Medam (April–May). The exact date changes every year.

title: Attukal Pongala
description: A ten-day festival whose main day sees millions of women prepare the ritual offering, recognised by Guinness World Records as the largest annual gathering of women for a religious purpose.
date_note: Held in the Malayalam month Kumbham (February–March). The main Pongala day is the ninth day. About 4 million took part in 2026.

title: Kochi-Muziris Biennale
venue: Fort Kochi, Mattancherry and other venues
description: India's largest contemporary art exhibition, held across heritage venues in Kochi.
date_note: Held every two years, usually opening on 12 December. The 6th edition ran 12 Dec 2025 – 31 Mar 2026. The next edition is listed for 2027; confirm dates with the Kochi Biennale Foundation.

title: International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK)
description: One of India's leading film festivals, run by the Kerala State Chalachitra Academy.
date_note: Usually held in December. The 30th edition ran 12–19 December 2025. One listing shows 11–18 December 2026; confirm on the official site.

title: Kerala Literature Festival
description: A four-day literature festival on Kozhikode Beach with authors and speakers from many countries.
date_note: Held in January in recent years. The 9th edition ran 22–25 January 2026. The next edition is listed for 21–24 January 2027 on Wikipedia but isn't officially confirmed.

title: Theyyam season
venue: Village shrines (kavus) across Kannur and Kasaragod
description: Ritual art performances in which performers embody deities, unique to North Malabar.
date_note: The season runs from late October or November to May or early June. The densest performances are between November and March.

title: Aranmula Uthrattathi Vallamkali
description: A ceremonial snake-boat water festival on the Pamba River during the Onam season.
date_note: Held on the Uthrattathi star in the Malayalam month Chingam (August–September). One source gives 27 September 2026 for this year, which is unconfirmed.

title: Cochin Carnival
description: New Year celebrations in Fort Kochi ending with the burning of the Pappanji effigy.
date_note: Culminates on New Year's Eve. Some years' events have been curtailed or cancelled, so check local announcements.

title: Sabarimala Mandalam–Makaravilakku season
description: The annual pilgrimage season at Sabarimala.
date_note: The 2026–27 season is expected to open on 16 or 17 November 2026 (sources differ), with Makaravilakku expected on 14 January 2027 and closing around 20 January. Dates are calculated, so confirm with the Travancore Devaswom Board.

title: Onam
description: Kerala's harvest festival: ten days of floral carpets, feasts, boat races and processions.
date_note: Celebrated in the Malayalam month Chingam (August–September) and ends on Thiruvonam. In 2026 the festival began on 16 August and Thiruvonam fell on 26 August. The Athachamayam procession in Thrippunithura opens the festival.

title: Kerala School Kalolsavam
description: The state's school arts festival, described as one of Asia's largest.
date_note: Usually held in December or January. The 63rd edition was held in Thiruvananthapuram on 4–8 January 2025 and the 64th in Thrissur on 14–18 January 2026.

title: Nenmara Vallanghy Vela
description: A temple festival where two villages stage caparisoned elephants facing each other, followed by a fireworks display.
date_note: Held on Meenam 20 in the Malayalam calendar, in early April. The Gregorian date shifts a little each year.
